description: General condition course, not an individual prognosis or confirmation of a screening label.

contact_dermatitis.text: Contact dermatitis can clear over days to weeks once the triggering substance is avoided. Some cases last longer or return with further exposure. This is a general range, not a personal recovery deadline. Get assessed if symptoms persist, worsen, keep returning, or are not responding to treatment.

atopic_dermatitis.text: Atopic dermatitis can have flare-ups and periods when symptoms are better. Treatment helps manage it, but there is no single number of days until it is permanently gone. A clinician can assess your symptoms and treatment response; a photo cannot predict your recovery time.

dermatitis.text: Dermatitis includes different types, so there is no single usual duration. Contact dermatitis may settle after its trigger is avoided; atopic dermatitis can flare and improve repeatedly. The type has not been confirmed here. A clinician can help identify it and assess persistent or worsening symptoms.

psoriasis.text: Psoriasis can have flare-ups and periods when symptoms are better. Treatment can help manage symptoms, but it does not have a fixed clearing time or a current cure. A clinician can assess your type of psoriasis and treatment response; a photo cannot predict how long your symptoms will last.

rosacea.text: Rosacea is a long-term condition. Symptoms can come and go, and treatment can help control them. There is no single time until it is permanently gone. A clinician can assess the symptoms and response to treatment; a photo cannot predict an individual recovery date.

lichen_planus.text: Lichen planus on the skin often improves over about 9 to 18 months, while mouth involvement can last several years. The affected area matters. These are general patterns, not a prediction for your skin; ask a clinician to confirm the condition and assess ongoing symptoms.

hives.text: Hives often improve within a few days, but they can keep returning. Seek medical advice if they do not improve after two days or keep recurring. This is general information, not a prediction of when your rash will resolve. Trouble breathing or swallowing or sudden mouth or tongue swelling needs emergency care.

normal_skin.text: A normal-skin screening match cannot identify the cause of symptoms or predict how long they will last. It does not confirm healthy skin. A clinician can assess persistent or worsening symptoms.
